IsAllowed.maps_to: RoundTeaParty.is_allowed (events/round_tea_party.py:29-31) `run.hp >= 12`, matching RoundTeaParty.cs:26-29's `p.Creature.CurrentHp >= 12`. The literal 12 is the source's, and it is deliberately ONE more than the 11 damage the fight branch deals -- the gate exists so the event can never be lethal, which is why EV-1 is dormant-by-gate here (see that guard). Quantifier collapses -- see the multiplayer guard.

guards.maps_to: events/round_tea_party.py:11 _DAMAGE = 11, and _MIN_HP = 12 for the gate. Both exact. The second CanonicalVar is a StringVar naming Royal Poison.

guards.what: EnjoyTea (RoundTeaParty.cs:40-46): RelicCmd.Obtain<RoyalPoison> FIRST, then Heal(MaxHp - CurrentHp) with both read AFTER the obtain
guards.maps_to: events/round_tea_party.py:39-42 add_relic('royal_poison') then `run.heal(run.max_hp - run.hp)`, reading both after the grant, which is what the source does -- it captures the Creature reference before the obtain but evaluates MaxHp/CurrentHp inside the Heal call (RoundTeaParty.cs:42-44). The order is only observable for a relic that moves max HP on pickup, and Royal Poison does not (relics/royal_poison.py has no after_obtained, only a turn-1 AfterPlayerTurnStart chip) -- but the sim preserves it anyway. This is a plain CreatureCmd.Heal, which dispatches no hooks in C# either (CreatureCmd.cs:691-703), so turn_structure step 38a does NOT apply -- confirmed by `py tools/audit/event_probes.py heal`, which lists this event under the plain-heal verb.

guards.what: PickFight (RoundTeaParty.cs:48-52) starts NO combat despite the name -- it is a SetEventState page with a single CONTINUE_FIGHT option
guards.maps_to: events/round_tea_party.py:44-45 `_set_state('PICK_FIGHT', [EventOption('CONTINUE_FIGHT', ...)])`. The sim correctly leaves pending_encounter unset; nothing here is an EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent.

events/round_tea_party.py:47-50 lose_hp(11) then obtain_relic_from_grab_bag(), which is run.py:631-636's pull_relic_from_front + add_relic -- the same Pull -> Obtain pair. Order preserved. The rarity roll is on the right stream: the source's one-argument PullNextRelicFromFront rolls on `player.PlayerRng.Rewards`, and obtain_relic_from_grab_bag with no rarity_rng falls through to run.rewards_rng (run.py:588-589, run.py:271-274), which is that stream. EV-3 does not apply.

guards.what: EV-1: ContinueFight's 11 HP loss (RoundTeaParty.cs:56) can reduce the player to 0 HP. C# routes event damage through CreatureCmd.Damage, whose Hook.ShouldDie / Hook.AfterPreventingDeath pass runs over RunState.IterateHookListeners (RunState.cs:545-596), which yields the POTION BELT outside combat; RunState.lose_hp (run.py:294-302) just subtracts
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-1, one verdict at all 18 lose_hp sites (rule 3). Fairy in a Bottle (FairyInABottle.cs:33-45: ShouldDie false for its owner, AfterPreventingDeath heals to max(MaxHp*0.3, 1)) IS ported (potions.py:1222-1250) and IS in the reward pool (potion_pools.py:49), but the sim's copy returns early when `self.combat is None` (potions.py:1246-1248) and is only registered as a listener by CombatState (combat.py:164-166), so it is inert during an event. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes.py lethal`): a run at 5 HP holding a belt Fairy that loses 15 HP ends DEAD at hp=-10 with the Fairy still in the belt; the game ends alive at 24 HP with the Fairy consumed. LIVE -- both sides ported and reachable, and the divergence ends the run. Secondary: run.lose_hp does not clamp at 0 either, so the sim carries negative HP.

guards.what: `runState.Players.All(...)` (RoundTeaParty.cs:28), the Royal Poison hover tip and the `.ThatDoesDamage(11)` annotation (RoundTeaParty.cs:35-36)
guards.rationale: multiplayer-only: the C# predicate is `runState.Players.All(p => ...)`, a quantifier over the party. The sim is single-player, so the quantifier collapses to the one player's clause, which the sim implements exactly. Out of scope per the shared contract's multiplayer waiver.

EventOption.ThatWontSaveToChoiceHistory (EventOption.cs:220) marks the option out of the run's MapPointHistory choice log. The sim has no choice-history subsystem at all, so there is nothing for the flag to switch off, and grep shows only three call sites in the whole source (RoundTeaParty.cs:50 and TheArchitect.cs:334, 339) -- all of them second-page 'continue' buttons, i.e. the flag exists so a history replay does not record a non-choice. Same observable game state; recorded as a divergence rather than a waiver because run history is not one of the contract's four out-of-scope categories, and a future history/telemetry port would need it. Same treatment as GoldLossType.Stolen on the morphic_grove record.
